language_wrapper: On a toroidal {rows} by {cols} chessboard (opposite edges identified), each square is colored black or white so that no two black squares are adjacent by a king’s move (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, with wrap-around). Among all such colorings having exactly {k} black squares, determine the number of valid colorings.
hardness_rationale: The seed problem counts independent sets on an n-by-n grid without horizontal/vertical adjacencies, solvable by a standard row-to-row transfer matrix with linear boundary. Our family imposes toroidal boundary conditions and prohibits king-adjacency (including diagonals), which forces compatibility constraints across wrap-around and necessitates tracking the first row to close the cycle. In addition, we require counting colorings with exactly k black squares, introducing a cardinality constraint. The natural solution is a two-dimensional transfer-matrix/dynamic programming with wrap-around closure and weight tracking, substantially more intricate than the seed and not amenable to guessing.
notes: Implementation uses bitmask states representing valid independent sets on a cycle (row), with precomputed compatibility edges enforcing vertical and diagonal constraints across consecutive rows. Wrap-around closure is handled by remembering the first row state and enforcing compatibility with the last row. The DP aggregates counts by total black-square cardinality, enabling exact-k queries. Generator selects parameters to ensure enough states and transitions for nontrivial difficulty.
source_question: The number of ways to color an \(n \times n\) chessboard with black and white such that no neighboring two blocks can be black simultaneously is \(x_n\). Find \(\sum_{n=2}^5 x_n\)．
